title: Rebase instead of merge
summary: Exercise 5: replay your commit on top of the new develop.

steps.title: Behind
steps.say: You branched a while ago, and develop moved on without you.

board.code:
develop        o---o---X        (X: a new commit)
issue-15            \--R      (your RAINBOW commit)

marks.label: your commit, based on old develop

steps.title: Rebase
steps.say: Rebasing **replays** your commits on top of develop's newest commit, as if you'd started there. No merge commit, a straight line.

marks.label: the same change, replayed on X

steps.title: The commands
steps.say: Stand on **your** branch and rebase it onto develop.

board.code:
git checkout issue-15-led-colors
git rebase develop
git log --oneline --graph --all

steps.title: Open a terminal
steps.say: These exercises are easiest in the terminal.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.say: `cd 05-rebase`, then run them. The graph should be one straight line.

steps.title: Merge or rebase?
steps.say: Rebase keeps history straight, but it **rewrites** your commits. Only rebase branches nobody else has pulled yet. When in doubt, merge.
